+"""End-to-end tests for interpreter mode, ``context``, settings, project

+configuration and the ``env`` commands."""

+

+import json

+import os

+import subprocess

+import sys

+import tempfile

+import textwrap

+import unittest

+

+SITH = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))), "sith.py")

+

+MAIN = '''\

+    import os

+

+

+    class Shape:

+        def area(self, scale):

+            total = scale

+            return total

+

+        async def grow(self):

+            def inner():

+                pass

+            return 1

+

+

+    def helper(a, b=2):

+        return a

+

+

+    local_value = 1

+    runtime_num

+    mod.

+    data.

+    mystery(

+    local_value

+    Obj.

+    '''

+

+NAMESPACES = [

+    {"runtime_num": {"type": "int", "value": "42"},

+     "runtime_other": {"type": "list"},

+     "mod": {"type": "module", "name": "os"},

+     "data": {"type": "dict"},

+     "mystery": {"type": "function", "value": "Does things."},

+     "local_value": {"type": "str"},

+     "Obj": {"type": "class", "module": "app", "attributes": ["alpha", "beta"]}},

+    {"runtime_num": {"type": "str"},

+     "runtime_late": {"type": "float"}},

+]

+

+

+class SithTestCase(unittest.TestCase):

+    def setUp(self):

+        self.directory = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()

+        self.root = os.path.realpath(self.directory.name)

+

+    def tearDown(self):

+        self.directory.cleanup()

+

+    def write(self, name, text):

+        path = os.path.join(self.root, name)

+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)

+        with open(path, "w") as handle:

+            handle.write(textwrap.dedent(text))

+        return path

+

+    def run_sith(self, *args, cwd=None, env=None):

+        return subprocess.run([sys.executable, SITH] + [str(a) for a in args],

+                              capture_output=True, text=True, cwd=cwd or self.root, env=env)

+

+    def json_of(self, *args, **kwargs):

+        completed = self.run_sith(*args, **kwargs)

+        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 0, completed.stderr)

+        return json.loads(completed.stdout)

+

+

+class InterpreterTest(SithTestCase):

+    def setUp(self):

+        super().setUp()

+        self.main = self.write("main.py", MAIN)

+        self.namespaces = self.write("ns.json", json.dumps(NAMESPACES))

+

+    def interpreter(self, command, line, col):

+        return self.json_of(command, self.main, line, col, "--interpreter",

+                            "--namespaces", self.namespaces)

+

+    def test_completion_merges_namespaces_first_match_wins(self):

+        found = self.interpreter("complete", 20, 8)["completions"]

+        by_name = {c["name"]: c for c in found}

+        self.assertEqual(by_name["runtime_num"],

+                         {"name": "runtime_num", "complete": "num", "type": "int",

+                          "description": "int (runtime)"})

+        self.assertEqual(by_name["runtime_other"]["description"], "list (runtime)")

+        self.assertEqual(by_name["runtime_late"]["type"], "float")

+

+    def test_static_names_win_over_namespaces(self):

+        found = self.interpreter("complete", 24, 5)["completions"]

+        local = [c for c in found if c["name"] == "local_value"]

+        self.assertEqual(local[0]["description"], "instance of int")

+        definitions = self.interpreter("infer", 24, 3)["definitions"]

+        self.assertEqual([d["name"] for d in definitions], ["int"])

+

+    def test_infer_and_goto_fall_back_to_namespaces(self):

+        for command in ("infer", "goto"):

+            definitions = self.interpreter(command, 20, 3)["definitions"]

+            self.assertEqual(len(definitions), 1)

+            self.assertEqual(definitions[0]["type"], "int")

+            self.assertEqual(definitions[0]["description"], "int (runtime)")

+            self.assertEqual(definitions[0]["docstring"], "42")

+

+    def test_attribute_completion_of_namespace_values(self):

+        names = [c["name"] for c in self.interpreter("complete", 21, 4)["completions"]]

+        self.assertIn("getcwd", names)

+        names = [c["name"] for c in self.interpreter("complete", 22, 5)["completions"]]

+        self.assertIn("keys", names)

+        names = [c["name"] for c in self.interpreter("complete", 25, 4)["completions"]]

+        self.assertEqual(names[:2], ["alpha", "beta"])

+

+    def test_signatures_of_namespace_function(self):

+        found = self.interpreter("signatures", 23, 8)["signatures"]

+        self.assertEqual(found[0]["name"], "mystery")

+        self.assertEqual(found[0]["docstring"], "Does things.")

+

+    def test_interpreter_without_namespaces_is_normal_mode(self):

+        normal = self.json_of("complete", self.main, 20, 8)

+        self.assertEqual(self.json_of("complete", self.main, 20, 8, "--interpreter"), normal)

+        self.assertEqual(normal["completions"], [])

+

+    def test_namespaces_without_interpreter_fails(self):

+        completed = self.run_sith("complete", self.main, 20, 7, "--namespaces", self.namespaces)

+        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)

+        self.assertTrue(completed.stderr)

+

+    def test_bad_namespaces_file_fails(self):

+        bad = self.write("bad.json", "{}")

+        completed = self.run_sith("complete", self.main, 20, 7, "--interpreter",

+                                  "--namespaces", bad)

+        self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1)

+

+

+class ContextTest(SithTestCase):

+    def setUp(self):

+        super().setUp()

+        self.main = self.write("main.py", MAIN)

+

+    def context(self, line, col):

+        return self.json_of("context", self.main, line, col)["context"]

+

+    def test_module_level_is_empty(self):

+        self.assertEqual(self.context(19, 0), [])

+

+    def test_nested_scopes_outermost_first(self):

+        self.assertEqual(self.context(6, 8), [

+            {"name": "Shape", "type": "class", "line": 4, "column": 6},

+            {"name": "area", "type": "function", "line": 5, "column": 8}])

+        self.assertEqual([s["name"] for s in self.context(11, 16)], ["Shape", "grow", "inner"])

+        self.assertEqual(self.context(16, 4),

+                         [{"name": "helper", "type": "function", "line": 15, "column": 4}])

+

+

+class SettingsTest(SithTestCase):

+    def setUp(self):

+        super().setUp()

+        self.main = self.write("m.py", '''\

+            def func(p):

+                return p

+

+

+            func(1)

+            Value = 1

+            value_two = 2

+            val

+            fu

+            ''')

+

+    def names(self, *extra):

+        found = self.json_of("complete", self.main, 8, 3, *extra)["completions"]

+        return [c["name"] for c in found]

+

+    def test_case_insensitive(self):

+        self.assertIn("Value", self.names())

+        self.assertEqual(self.names("--setting", "case_insensitive=false"), ["value_two"])

+        self.assertIn("Value", self.names("--setting", "case_insensitive=TRUE"))

+

+    def test_add_bracket(self):

+        found = self.json_of("complete", self.main, 9, 2, "--setting", "add_bracket=true")

+        func = [c for c in found["completions"] if c["name"] == "func"][0]

+        self.assertEqual(func["complete"], "nc(")

+

+    def test_dynamic_params(self):

+        self.assertEqual(len(self.json_of("infer", self.main, 2, 12)["definitions"]), 1)

+        found = self.json_of("infer", self.main, 2, 12, "--setting", "dynamic_params=false")

+        self.assertEqual(found["definitions"], [])

+

+    def test_invalid_settings_fail(self):

+        for setting in ("nonsense=true", "add_bracket=maybe", "add_bracket"):

+            completed = self.run_sith("complete", self.main, 8, 3, "--setting", setting)

+            self.assertEqual(completed.returncode, 1, setting)

+

+    def test_cli_overrides_project_config(self):

+        os.makedirs(os.path.join(self.root, ".sith"))

+        self.write(".sith/project.json", '{"case_insensitive": false}')

+        self.assertEqual(self.names(), ["value_two"])

+        self.assertIn("Value", self.names("--setting", "case_insensitive=true"))

+

+

+class ProjectTest(SithTestCase):

+    def setUp(self):

+        super().setUp()

+        self.write("src/mylib/__init__.py", "def libfunc():\n    pass\n")

+        self.write("extra/extramod.py", "EXTRA = 1\n")

+        self.write("app/sibling.py", "SIB = 1\n")

+        self.main = self.write("app/main.py", '''\

+            import mylib

+            import extramod

+            import sibling

+            mylib.libfunc

+            extramod.EXTRA

+            sibling.SIB

+            ''')

+

+    def config(self):

+        with open(os.path.join(self.root, ".sith", "project.json")) as handle:

+            return json.load(handle)

+

+    def resolves(self, line, col):

+        found = self.json_of("infer", self.main, line, col, "--project", self.root)

+        return bool(found["definitions"])

+

+    def test_init_defaults_and_merge(self):

+        self.json_of("project", "init")

+        self.assertEqual(self.config(), {"environment_path": "", "sys_path": [],

+                                         "added_sys_path": [], "smart_sys_path": True})

+        self.json_of("project", "init", self.root, "--environment", "/usr/bin/python3")

+        self.json_of("project", "init", self.root, "--added-sys-path", "a,b")

+        self.assertEqual(self.config(), {"environment_path": "/usr/bin/python3",

+                                         "sys_path": [], "added_sys_path": ["a", "b"],

+                                         "smart_sys_path": True})

+

+    def test_init_creates_directory(self):

+        target = os.path.join(self.root, "new")

+        self.json_of("project", "init", target, "--sys-path", "x")

+        self.assertTrue(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(target, ".sith", "project.json")))

+

+    def test_added_sys_path(self):

+        self.assertFalse(self.resolves(4, 7))

+        self.json_of("project", "init", "--added-sys-path", "src")

+        self.assertTrue(self.resolves(4, 7))

+        found = self.json_of("infer", self.main, 4, 7, "--project", self.root)

+        self.assertEqual(found["definitions"][0]["full_name"], "mylib.libfunc")

+

+    def test_sys_path_replaces_auto_detection(self):

+        self.assertTrue(self.resolves(6, 9))

+        self.json_of("project", "init", "--sys-path", "extra")

+        self.assertTrue(self.resolves(5, 10))

+        self.assertFalse(self.resolves(6, 9))

+

+    def test_smart_sys_path_false(self):

+        self.json_of("project", "init", "--added-sys-path", "src",

+                     "--setting", "smart_sys_path=false")

+        self.assertIs(self.config()["smart_sys_path"], False)

+        self.assertTrue(self.resolves(4, 7))

+        self.assertFalse(self.resolves(6, 9))

+        found = self.json_of("infer", self.main, 6, 9, "--project", self.root,

+                             "--setting", "smart_sys_path=true")

+        self.assertTrue(found["definitions"])

+

+

+class EnvTest(SithTestCase):

+    def test_list(self):

+        environments = self.json_of("env", "list")["environments"]

+        self.assertTrue(environments)

+        for environment in environments:

+            self.assertEqual(set(environment), {"executable", "version", "is_virtualenv"})

+            self.assertTrue(os.path.isabs(environment["executable"]))

+        resolved = [os.path.realpath(e["executable"]) for e in environments]

+        self.assertEqual(len(resolved), len(set(resolved)))

+        self.assertIn(os.path.realpath(sys.executable), resolved)

+        keys = [(tuple(-int(p) for p in e["version"].split(".")), e["executable"])

+                for e in environments]

+        self.assertEqual(keys, sorted(keys))

+

+    def test_find_virtualenvs(self):

+        venvs = os.path.join(self.root, "venvs")

+        subprocess.run([sys.executable, "-m", "venv", "--without-pip",

+                        os.path.join(venvs, "real")], check=True)

+        self.write("venvs/fake/pyvenv.cfg", "version = 3.9.1\n")

+        self.write("venvs/fake/bin/python", "")

+        self.write("venvs/plain/readme.txt", "")

+        env = dict(os.environ, HOME=self.root)

+        found = self.json_of("env", "find-virtualenvs", "--path", venvs, env=env)

+        found = found["environments"]

+        self.assertEqual([e["executable"] for e in found],

+                         [os.path.join(venvs, "real", "bin", "python"),

+                          os.path.join(venvs, "fake", "bin", "python")])

+        self.assertTrue(all(e["is_virtualenv"] for e in found))

+        self.assertEqual(found[1]["version"], "3.9.1")

+

+    def test_info(self):

+        info = self.json_of("env", "info", sys.executable)

+        self.assertEqual(info["version"], "%d.%d.%d" % sys.version_info[:3])

+        self.assertEqual(info["prefix"], sys.prefix)

+        self.assertEqual(info["is_virtualenv"], sys.prefix != sys.base_prefix)

+        self.assertIsInstance(info["sys_path"], list)

+        self.assertIn("prefix", self.json_of("env", "info"))

+

+    def test_info_rejects_non_python(self):

+        missing = self.run_sith("env", "info", os.path.join(self.root, "nope"))

+        self.assertEqual(missing.returncode, 1)

+        other = self.write("not_python", "")

+        self.assertEqual(self.run_sith("env", "info", other).returncode, 1)

+

+

+if __name__ == "__main__":

+    unittest.main()

+class NamespaceValue(Value):

+    """The value of an interpreter namespace entry. Its members are those of

+    the object it can be traced to (a module or a module attribute, or for an

+    instance, its builtin type) plus the attributes the entry lists."""

+

+    def __init__(self, project, name, entry):

+        self.project = project

+        self.name = name

+        self.entry = entry

+        self.kind = _NAMESPACE_KINDS.get(entry.type, INSTANCE)

+        self.type_name = entry.type

+        self._backing = None

+

+    def key(self):

+        return ("namespace", self.name, id(self.entry))

+

+    def backing(self):

+        """Values of the object this entry describes, as far as they are known."""

+        if self._backing is None:

+            self._backing = []

+            if self.project.enter(self.key()):

+                try:

+                    self._backing = self._find_backing()

+                finally:

+                    self.project.leave(self.key())

+        return list(self._backing)

+

+    def _find_backing(self):

+        entry = self.entry

+        if self.kind == INSTANCE:

+            cls = getattr(builtins, entry.type, None)

+            if isinstance(cls, type):

+                return [RuntimeInstance(self.project, cls)]

+            module = self.project.module_value(entry.module) if entry.module else None

+            if module is None:

+                return []

+            return [i for c in module.attribute(entry.type) if c.kind == CLASS

+                    for i in c.instantiate()]

+        if self.kind == MODULE:

+            for dotted in dict.fromkeys(n for n in (entry.name, entry.module, self.name) if n):

+                found = self.project.module_value(dotted)

+                if found is not None and found.kind == MODULE:

+                    return [found]

+            return []

+        if not entry.module:

+            return []

+        module = self.project.module_value(entry.module)

+        if module is None:

+            return []

+        return [v for v in module.attribute(entry.name or self.name) if v.kind == self.kind]

+

+    def members(self):

+        result = {}

+        for value in self.backing():

+            for name, entity in value.members().items():

+                result.setdefault(name, entity)

+        for name in self.entry.attributes:

+            result.setdefault(name, ValueEntity(name, lambda n=name: self._attribute(n)))

+        return result

+

+    def _attribute(self, name):

+        return [v for value in self.backing() for v in value.attribute(name)]

+

+    def attribute(self, name):

+        return _unique(self._attribute(name))

+

+    def attribute_targets(self, name):

+        found = [t for value in self.backing() for t in value.attribute_targets(name)]

+        if not found and name in self.entry.attributes:

+            found = [ValueEntity(name, lambda: self._attribute(name))]

+        return found

+

+    def call(self, arguments=None):

+        return _unique([v for value in self.backing() for v in value.call(arguments)])

+

+    def instantiate(self):

+        return _unique([v for value in self.backing() for v in value.instantiate()])

+

+    def iterate(self):

+        return _unique([v for value in self.backing() for v in value.iterate()])

+

+    def subscript(self, index):

+        return _unique([v for value in self.backing() for v in value.subscript(index)])

+

+    def builtin_type(self):

+        for value in self.backing():

+            found = value.builtin_type()

+            if found is not None:

+                return found

+        return None

+

+"""Python environment discovery.

+

+Secret: where Python installations and virtualenvs are looked for (the

+running interpreter, ``PATH``, conventional install and virtualenv

+locations), how an executable is asked about itself (a subprocess printing

+its version, prefixes and ``sys.path``), what makes it a virtualenv, and how

+found environments are deduplicated and ordered.

+"""

+

+import json

+import os

+import re

+import shutil

+import subprocess

+import sys

+

+_WINDOWS = os.name == "nt"

+_EXECUTABLE = re.compile(r"^python(\d+(\.\d+)?)?(\.exe)?$", re.IGNORECASE)

+_PROBE = (

+    "import json, sys\n"

+    "print(json.dumps({'version': '%d.%d.%d' % tuple(sys.version_info[:3]),"

+    " 'prefix': sys.prefix,"

+    " 'base_prefix': getattr(sys, 'base_prefix', sys.prefix),"

+    " 'real_prefix': getattr(sys, 'real_prefix', None),"

+    " 'sys_path': sys.path}))\n"

+)

+_TIMEOUT = 15

+

+

+class Environment:

+    def __init__(self, executable, version, is_virtualenv, prefix=None, sys_path=None):

+        self.executable = executable

+        self.version = version

+        self.is_virtualenv = is_virtualenv

+        self.prefix = prefix

+        self.sys_path = sys_path or []

+

+    def summary(self):

+        return {"executable": self.executable, "version": self.version,

+                "is_virtualenv": self.is_virtualenv}

+

+    def details(self):

+        return dict(self.summary(), prefix=self.prefix, sys_path=list(self.sys_path))

+

+

+_PROBED = {}

+

+

+def probe(executable):

+    """The Environment of the Python at path ``executable``, or None when it

+    is not a working Python interpreter."""

+    executable = os.path.abspath(executable)

+    if executable in _PROBED:

+        return _PROBED[executable]

+    found = None

+    if os.path.isfile(executable) and os.access(executable, os.X_OK):

+        try:

+            completed = subprocess.run([executable, "-c", _PROBE], stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,

+                                       stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL,

+                                       timeout=_TIMEOUT, cwd=os.path.dirname(executable))

+            data = json.loads(completed.stdout.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")

+                              .strip().splitlines()[-1]) if completed.returncode == 0 else None

+        except (OSError, ValueError, IndexError, subprocess.SubprocessError):

+            data = None

+        if isinstance(data, dict) and isinstance(data.get("version"), str):

+            prefix = data.get("prefix")

+            virtual = bool(data.get("real_prefix")) or (

+                prefix is not None and prefix != data.get("base_prefix"))

+            paths = [p for p in data.get("sys_path") or [] if isinstance(p, str) and p]

+            found = Environment(executable, data["version"], virtual, prefix, paths)

+    _PROBED[executable] = found

+    return found

+

+

+def find_executable(name):

+    """Absolute path of the executable called (or found at) ``name``, or None."""

+    if os.sep in name or (os.altsep and os.altsep in name):

+        return os.path.abspath(name) if os.path.isfile(name) else None

+    found = shutil.which(name)

+    return os.path.abspath(found) if found else None

+

+

+def default_executable():

+    return find_executable("python3") or find_executable("python") or sys.executable

+

+

+def system_environments():

+    """Python installations on this system (newest first)."""

+    found = []

+    seen = set()

+    for executable in _system_candidates():

+        key = os.path.realpath(executable)

+        if key in seen:

+            continue

+        environment = probe(executable)

+        if environment is not None:

+            seen.add(key)

+            found.append(environment)

+    return _ordered(found)

+

+

+def virtualenvs(path=None, project_root=None):

+    """Virtualenvs below ``path`` and in the conventional locations (newest first)."""

+    directories = []

+    if path:

+        directories += _subdirectories(path)

+    directories += _subdirectories(os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".virtualenvs"))

+    for base in dict.fromkeys([os.getcwd(), project_root or os.getcwd()]):

+        directories += [os.path.join(base, ".venv"), os.path.join(base, "venv")]

+    found = []

+    seen = set()

+    for directory in directories:

+        key = os.path.realpath(directory)

+        if key in seen:

+            continue

+        environment = _virtualenv(directory)

+        if environment is not None:

+            seen.add(key)

+            found.append(environment)

+    return _ordered(found)

+

+

+def site_directories(executable):

+    """The package directories (``site-packages``) on the ``sys.path`` of the

+    Python at ``executable``."""

+    environment = probe(executable) if executable else None

+    if environment is None:

+        return []

+    return [p for p in environment.sys_path

+            if os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(p)) in ("site-packages", "dist-packages")

+            and os.path.isdir(p)]

+

+

+def _virtualenv(directory):

+    if not os.path.isdir(directory):

+        return None

+    if _WINDOWS:

+        names = [os.path.join("Scripts", "python.exe")]

+    else:

+        names = [os.path.join("bin", "python"), os.path.join("bin", "python3")]

+    for name in names:

+        executable = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(directory, name))

+        if not os.path.isfile(executable):

+            continue

+        environment = probe(executable)

+        if environment is not None:

+            return Environment(executable, environment.version, True,

+                               environment.prefix, environment.sys_path)

+        version = _configured_version(directory)

+        if version is not None:

+            return Environment(executable, version, True, os.path.abspath(directory))

+    return None

+

+

+def _configured_version(directory):

+    """The Python version recorded in a virtualenv's ``pyvenv.cfg``, or None."""

+    try:

+        with open(os.path.join(directory, "pyvenv.cfg"), encoding="utf-8",

+                  errors="replace") as handle:

+            lines = handle.read().splitlines()

+    except OSError:

+        return None

+    for line in lines:

+        key, sep, value = line.partition("=")

+        if sep and key.strip() in ("version", "version_info") and value.strip():

+            return value.strip()

+    return None

+

+

+def _subdirectories(path):

+    try:

+        names = sorted(os.listdir(path))

+    except OSError:

+        return []

+    return [os.path.join(path, name) for name in names

+            if os.path.isdir(os.path.join(path, name))]

+

+

+def _system_candidates():

+    candidates = []

+    directories = os.environ.get("PATH", "").split(os.pathsep)

+    if _WINDOWS:

+        directories += [os.path.join(os.environ.get("LOCALAPPDATA", ""), "Programs", "Python")]

+    else:

+        directories += ["/usr/local/bin", "/usr/bin", "/bin", "/opt/homebrew/bin",

+                        "/opt/local/bin"]

+        directories += [os.path.join(d, "bin") for d in _subdirectories(

+            os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".pyenv", "versions"))]

+    for directory in dict.fromkeys(d for d in directories if d):

+        try:

+            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory))

+        except OSError:

+            continue

+        for name in names:

+            if _EXECUTABLE.match(name):

+                candidates.append(os.path.abspath(os.path.join(directory, name)))

+    if sys.executable:  # the running interpreter, when not found otherwise

+        candidates.append(os.path.abspath(sys.executable))

+    return candidates

+

+

+def _version_key(version):

+    numbers = []

+    for part in re.split(r"[.\-+]", version):

+        match = re.match(r"\d+", part)

+        numbers.append(int(match.group()) if match else 0)

+    return tuple(numbers)

+

+

+def _ordered(environments):

+    environments = sorted(environments, key=lambda e: e.executable)

+    return sorted(environments, key=lambda e: _version_key(e.version), reverse=True)

+"""Interpreter namespaces.

+

+Secret: the format of a namespaces file (a JSON array of objects mapping

+names to descriptions of runtime values with ``type``, ``value``,

+``module``, ``name`` and ``attributes`` fields) and how a malformed file or

+entry is treated (the file is rejected; an odd entry is read leniently).

+"""

+

+import json

+

+

+class NamespaceError(Exception):

+    """The namespaces file cannot be used."""

+

+

+class Entry:

+    """What is known about one runtime value."""

+

+    def __init__(self, type_name, value=None, module=None, name=None, attributes=()):

+        self.type = type_name

+        self.value = value

+        self.module = module

+        self.name = name

+        self.attributes = list(attributes)

+

+    def full_name(self, key):

+        name = self.name or key

+        if self.module and self.type != "module":

+            return "%s.%s" % (self.module, name)

+        return name

+

+

+def load(path):

+    """The namespaces stored in the file at ``path``: a list of dicts mapping

+    names to Entry objects, in search order."""

+    try:

+        with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+            data = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8-sig"))

+    except OSError as exc:

+        raise NamespaceError("cannot read namespaces file %s: %s" % (path, exc))

+    except ValueError as exc:

+        raise NamespaceError("namespaces file %s is not valid JSON: %s" % (path, exc))

+    if not isinstance(data, list) or not all(isinstance(n, dict) for n in data):

+        raise NamespaceError("namespaces file %s must hold a JSON array of objects" % path)

+    return [{name: _entry(description) for name, description in namespace.items()}

+            for namespace in data]

+

+

+def _entry(description):

+    if isinstance(description, str):

+        return Entry(description)

+    if not isinstance(description, dict):

+        return Entry(type(description).__name__ if description is not None else "NoneType",

+                     value=json.dumps(description))

+    type_name = description.get("type")

+    attributes = description.get("attributes")

+    return Entry(type_name if isinstance(type_name, str) and type_name else "object",

+                 value=_text(description.get("value")),

+                 module=_text(description.get("module")),

+                 name=_text(description.get("name")),

+                 attributes=[a for a in attributes if isinstance(a, str)]

+                 if isinstance(attributes, list) else ())

+

+

+def _text(value):

+    if value is None:

+        return None

+    return value if isinstance(value, str) else json.dumps(value)

+"""Settings and project configuration.

+

+Secret: which settings exist and how their values are spelled on the command

+line, where a project's persistent configuration lives (``.sith/project.json``

+below the project root) and how it is read, merged and written, and the

+precedence of command-line settings over project configuration over defaults.

+The settings of the running command are kept as the *active* settings.

+"""

+

+import json

+import os

+

+CONFIG_DIRECTORY = ".sith"

+CONFIG_FILE = "project.json"

+

+# Settings accepted by ``--setting key=value`` (all boolean).

+SETTINGS = {

+    "case_insensitive": True,

+    "dynamic_params": True,

+    "smart_sys_path": True,

+    "add_bracket": False,

+}

+

+# Fields of a project configuration file, with their defaults.

+PROJECT_FIELDS = {

+    "environment_path": "",

+    "sys_path": [],

+    "added_sys_path": [],

+    "smart_sys_path": True,

+}

+

+

+class ConfigError(Exception):

+    """A setting or configuration value is malformed."""

+

+

+class Settings:

+    """The effective configuration of one command."""

+

+    def __init__(self, root=None, values=None, project=None):

+        values = dict(SETTINGS, **(values or {}))

+        project = dict(_project_defaults(), **(project or {}))

+        self.root = os.path.abspath(root) if root else None

+        self.case_insensitive = values["case_insensitive"]

+        self.dynamic_params = values["dynamic_params"]

+        self.smart_sys_path = values["smart_sys_path"]

+        self.add_bracket = values["add_bracket"]

+        self.environment_path = project["environment_path"] or None

+        self.sys_path = [self._absolute(p) for p in project["sys_path"]]

+        self.added_sys_path = [self._absolute(p) for p in project["added_sys_path"]]

+

+    def _absolute(self, path):

+        path = os.path.expanduser(path)

+        if not os.path.isabs(path) and self.root:

+            path = os.path.join(self.root, path)

+        return os.path.normpath(os.path.abspath(path))

+

+

+_ACTIVE = None

+

+

+def activate(settings):

+    global _ACTIVE

+    _ACTIVE = settings

+

+

+def active():

+    """The settings of the running command (the defaults until activated)."""

+    global _ACTIVE

+    if _ACTIVE is None:

+        _ACTIVE = Settings()

+    return _ACTIVE

+

+

+def parse_setting(text):

+    """``(key, value)`` for a ``key=value`` command-line setting."""

+    key, sep, raw = text.partition("=")

+    key = key.strip()

+    if not sep or key not in SETTINGS:

+        raise ConfigError("unknown setting: %s" % text)

+    value = _boolean(raw.strip())

+    if value is None:

+        raise ConfigError("setting %s needs true or false, not %r" % (key, raw))

+    return key, value

+

+

+def resolve(root, overrides):

+    """The settings for a command run in project ``root`` (may be None) with

+    command-line ``overrides`` (dict of setting -> value)."""

+    project = load_project(root) if root else {}

+    values = {key: project[key] for key in SETTINGS if isinstance(project.get(key), bool)}

+    values.update(overrides)

+    return Settings(root, values, {key: project[key] for key in PROJECT_FIELDS

+                                   if key in project})

+

+

+def config_path(root):

+    return os.path.join(root, CONFIG_DIRECTORY, CONFIG_FILE)

+

+

+def load_project(root):

+    """The valid entries of the configuration stored for project ``root`` (a

+    dict; empty when there is none or it cannot be read)."""

+    try:

+        with open(config_path(root), "rb") as handle:

+            data = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))

+    except (OSError, ValueError):

+        return {}

+    if not isinstance(data, dict):

+        return {}

+    found = {}

+    environment = data.get("environment_path")

+    if environment is None or isinstance(environment, str):

+        found["environment_path"] = environment

+    for key in ("sys_path", "added_sys_path"):

+        paths = data.get(key)

+        if isinstance(paths, list) and all(isinstance(p, str) for p in paths):

+            found[key] = list(paths)

+    for key in SETTINGS:

+        value = data.get(key)

+        if isinstance(value, str):

+            value = _boolean(value)

+        if isinstance(value, bool):

+            found[key] = value

+    return found

+

+

+def init_project(directory, updates):

+    """Create or update the configuration of project ``directory`` with the

+    fields in ``updates``; return ``(path, configuration)``."""

+    path = config_path(directory)

+    existing = {}

+    try:

+        with open(path, "rb") as handle:

+            existing = json.loads(handle.read().decode("utf-8"))

+    except (OSError, ValueError):

+        existing = {}

+    if not isinstance(existing, dict):

+        existing = {}

+    configuration = dict(_project_defaults(), **existing)

+    configuration.update(updates)

+    try:

+        os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(path), exist_ok=True)

+        with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:

+            json.dump(configuration, handle, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)

+            handle.write("\n")

+    except OSError as exc:

+        raise ConfigError("cannot write %s: %s" % (path, exc))

+    return path, configuration

+

+

+def split_paths(text):

+    """The entries of a comma-separated path list."""

+    return [part.strip() for part in text.split(",") if part.strip()]

+

+

+def _boolean(text):

+    lowered = text.lower()

+    if lowered == "true":

+        return True

+    if lowered == "false":

+        return False

+    return None

+

+

+def _project_defaults():

+    return {key: list(value) if isinstance(value, list) else value

+            for key, value in PROJECT_FIELDS.items()}
